tips.title: After a traffic accident, stop, help the injured, and call the police — don’t flee
tips.cost: No cost. Call 112, ask for an ambulance if needed, and give your details. Do not move an injured person unless there is a fire or traffic danger.
tips.inPlainWords: After a road accident you must stop, help the injured and report to the police. Driving away is an offence. Section 134 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 requires the driver to stop, give his name and address, and report the accident; the BNS, 2023 punishes rash or negligent driving and causing death by negligence. Call 112, move the injured only if there is immediate danger, and take photographs before the vehicles are moved.
tips.benefit: The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 requires a driver involved in an accident to stop, give identification and report to the nearest police station. The BNS, 2023 contains offences for causing death by negligence and for rash driving. Section 134A of the Motor Vehicles Act protects a Good Samaritan who helps an injured person from civil or criminal liability for acting in good faith. The insurer may be notified, and the FIR is the basis for the claim. Fleeing turns a compensation case into a criminal one.
tips.sources: Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (sections 134, 134A, 161). <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Ministry of Road Transport and Highways. <https://morth.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: Do not sign a settlement at the roadside before the injury is assessed. A hit-and-run is treated more seriously than a reported accident. If you are the victim, note the vehicle number and keep the medical records.

tips.title: If you realize you’ve been scammed, call 112 or 1930 (cyber fraud) right away to request a stop‑payment — don’t try to investigate on your own first.
tips.cost: No cost. Keep the transaction ID, the chat, the caller number and the account details. Inform the bank in writing and keep the acknowledgement.
tips.inPlainWords: If you realise you have been scammed, call 1930 and file a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in at once, then inform your bank and ask it to freeze the beneficiary account. A report filed within the first hours has the best chance of stopping the transfer. Do not argue with the scammer or send more money to 'release' the first payment.
tips.benefit: The National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal and the 1930 helpline feed a financial-fraud reporting system that lets banks freeze a beneficiary account. The RBI's customer-protection rules require a bank to act on a fraud report, and the BNS, 2023 and the IT Act cover cheating and identity misuse. A quick written complaint to the bank, with the transaction reference, is stronger than a phone call. A delayed report gives the money time to move.
tips.sources: National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal. <https://cybercrime.gov.in/>; Reserve Bank of India, customer protection. <https://www.rbi.org.in/>; Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: Recovery is not guaranteed, especially if the money has moved abroad. Do not pay a 'recovery agent' who asks for an upfront fee. If the fraud used your Aadhaar or PAN, inform the tax department and the UIDAI as well.

tips.title: Remember the core anti-fraud rules: don’t trust unsolicited calls, don’t share personal information, don’t click on suspicious links, and always verify any transfer requests. All seven of the most common scam types follow this same pattern.
tips.cost: No cost. Hang up, verify on the official app or a known number, and report on 1930. Install the bank's official app and enable transaction alerts.
tips.inPlainWords: The core rules are simple: do not trust an unsolicited call, do not share an OTP, PIN or password, do not click a link in an SMS, and do not move money because a caller says the account is blocked. A bank or the police never ask for an OTP. If the call is about a 'safe account', it is a scam.
tips.benefit: Phishing, vishing and 'digital arrest' scams use the same pressure: urgency, secrecy and a request for money or credentials. The RBI and banks state that they never ask for an OTP, PIN or password. The IT Act, 2000 and the BNS, 2023 cover identity theft and cheating. A genuine notice is visible in the official app or portal, not in a link from an unknown number.
tips.sources: Reserve Bank of India, awareness. <https://www.rbi.org.in/>; National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal. <https://cybercrime.gov.in/>; Information Technology Act, 2000. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: A caller can show a bank's name on the screen with caller-ID spoofing. A video call does not prove identity. Do not install a screen-sharing app at a caller's request.

tips.title: Seeing a face on video or hearing a voice on the phone does not count as verification; if a transfer is involved, hang up first and call back using an old number saved in your contacts.
tips.cost: No cost. Keep a family 'safe word' and a written list of numbers. Do not trust a video call alone.
tips.inPlainWords: A familiar face on video or a familiar voice on the phone is not proof of identity. Deepfakes and voice clones are cheap now. If the call involves a transfer, hang up and call back on a number you already have, or ask a mutual acquaintance. A request for secrecy or urgency is a warning sign.
tips.benefit: The IT Act, 2000 and the BNS, 2023 punish cheating by personation and identity theft. The MeitY advisories require platforms to label synthetic or AI-generated content, but a label cannot be relied on because a criminal will not add one. Cross-channel verification — a callback on a stored number, a question only the real person can answer, a second family contact — is the reliable test.
tips.sources: National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal. <https://cybercrime.gov.in/>; Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, AI advisories. <https://www.meity.gov.in/>; Information Technology Act, 2000. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: A short video can be recorded or generated. A request to install an app or share a screen is a red flag. If money has gone, call 1930 at once.

tips.title: If accused or summoned, hire a lawyer first — don’t settle privately or delete records
tips.cost: A lawyer costs money; legal aid is available through NALSA on 15100 or the district legal services authority. Do not pay a 'contact' to fix the case.
tips.inPlainWords: If the police accuse or summon you, speak to a lawyer before you make a statement. The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 gives you the right to be informed of the grounds and to consult a lawyer, and the right to remain silent. Do not delete messages, transfer assets or 'settle' privately with the complainant; that can look like destruction of evidence or interference.
tips.benefit: The BNSS, 2023 sets out the procedure for arrest, bail and the production of an arrested person before a magistrate within 24 hours. A confession to a police officer is not admissible in evidence; a statement before a magistrate has its own safeguards. The BNS, 2023 punishes destroying evidence and obstructing a public servant. A lawyer can apply for anticipatory bail where the offence is eligible.
tips.sources: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; National Legal Services Authority. <https://nalsa.gov.in/>; Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: A summons must be in writing and state the offence. Ask for a copy. A phone call is not a summons. If you cannot afford a lawyer, apply for legal aid at the court.

tips.title: Coming forward voluntarily after an incident: Self‑surrender can cut a sentence by up to 40%, and the “statute of limitations” defense simply does not exist
tips.cost: A lawyer's fee; legal aid is available. Do not pay an intermediary who promises a 'settlement' with the police.
tips.inPlainWords: If you have done something wrong, a voluntary surrender and cooperation can help at sentencing, but there is no fixed discount. The Limitation Act, 1963 sets time limits for civil claims; criminal prosecution has its own limitation under the BNSS. Speak to a lawyer before you approach the police; a written surrender through counsel protects your rights.
tips.benefit: The BNSS, 2023 sets the limitation periods for offences and the procedure for surrender and bail. A court may take cooperation into account, but the sentence depends on the offence and the facts. The Limitation Act, 1963 bars a civil suit after the prescribed period, subject to condonation. A lawyer can advise on anticipatory bail and on whether a prosecution is time-barred.
tips.sources: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Limitation Act, 1963. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; National Legal Services Authority. <https://nalsa.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: A surrender is not a guarantee of a lighter sentence. Do not make a statement without a lawyer. A civil limitation period can be extended in some cases, but not as a rule.

tips.title: Do not drive after drinking — not a car, not a scooter, not 'just moving it a bit'
tips.cost: The fine, the lawyer and the lost licence cost far more than a cab. Book a taxi or a sober driver before you drink.
tips.inPlainWords: Driving with alcohol above the legal limit is an offence under section 185 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, and causing death by drunken driving is punished under the BNS, 2023. The licence can be suspended or cancelled, the insurer can refuse the claim, and a conviction can affect a job or a visa. 'Just moving the car' is still driving.
tips.benefit: Section 185 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 punishes driving by a person with alcohol above 30 mg per 100 ml of blood. Section 184 punishes dangerous driving, and the BNS, 2023 punishes causing death by negligence. A court can suspend the licence and order a fine or imprisonment. The insurer can treat the policy as void for a drunken-driving claim. A commercial licence can be cancelled.
tips.sources: Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (sections 184, 185, 187). <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Ministry of Road Transport and Highways. <https://morth.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: A small amount can still be over the limit depending on body weight and time. A breathalyser test is evidence; refusing a lawful test has consequences. Do not rely on coffee or a cold shower.

tips.title: Never lend your bank cards, SIM cards, or payment accounts to anyone — “money laundering” is not a side hustle
tips.cost: No cost. Never share the card, PIN, OTP or net-banking login, and never let anyone else operate your account.
tips.inPlainWords: Lending, renting or selling your bank account, SIM card or payment account is an offence in itself. It is the classic money-mule route: the account receives the proceeds of fraud and you are the named holder. Banks freeze such accounts, and the BNS, 2023, the PMLA, 2002 and the IT Act can apply. A small commission is not worth a criminal record.
tips.benefit: The BNS, 2023 covers cheating and dishonest receiving; the PMLA, 2002 allows attachment and prosecution; the IT Act covers unauthorised access. The RBI's KYC rules require the bank to monitor and report suspicious accounts. A frozen account stops your salary, your UPI and your credit. The account holder can be called for questioning even if someone else operated the account.
tips.sources: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Reserve Bank of India, KYC. <https://www.rbi.org.in/>; National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal. <https://cybercrime.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: A family member asking to use your account for a 'business' payment is still a risk. If your account is frozen, contact the bank and the cyber police; do not try to move the money.

tips.title: Checking your credit report twice a year for free helps spot any loans or cards you didn’t apply for.
tips.cost: The annual report is free. A paid subscription is optional. Disputes are free.
tips.inPlainWords: Check your credit report at least twice a year. The RBI requires credit information companies to give you one free full report a year, and a loan or card you did not apply for will show up there. A wrong entry should be disputed with the lender and the credit bureau in writing.
tips.benefit: The Credit Information (Companies) Regulation Act, 2005 and the RBI directions govern credit bureaus. A free report is available from each bureau once a year. A new loan enquiry, a default or a card you do not recognise can be an identity theft signal. The lender must correct a genuine error, and the RBI's grievance redressal route can be used if it does not.
tips.sources: Reserve Bank of India, credit information. <https://www.rbi.org.in/>; TransUnion CIBIL. <https://www.cibil.com/>; Credit Information (Companies) Regulation Act, 2005. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: A hard enquiry can lower your score slightly. Do not share your credit report with an agent who asks for an OTP. A closed loan may still show as open for a month.

tips.title: If a conflict breaks out, call the police first and do not strike: whoever strikes first makes it easy for the other party's counterstrike to be ruled lawful self-defense
tips.cost: No cost to walk away. A lawyer, a medical report and a settlement cost far more.
tips.inPlainWords: If a quarrel starts, call 112 and move away. Do not strike first. The BNS, 2023 punishes hurt and criminal intimidation, and a fight that starts with a push can end with a criminal case. A witness and a written complaint are stronger than a punch.
tips.benefit: The BNS, 2023 distinguishes simple hurt, grievous hurt and hurt by a dangerous weapon, with heavier penalties for each. The right of private defence is available only against an immediate threat and only with proportionate force. The BNSS, 2023 allows the police to register an FIR and, where the offence is compoundable, the parties may settle with the court's permission. A first strike is not self-defence.
tips.sources: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: Do not record and upload the fight; it can be evidence against you. If you are injured, get a medical examination and a copy of the report.

tips.title: You may defend yourself against an unavoidable attack, but only strike the person who is actually attacking — stop when he stops.
tips.cost: No cost. Call 112 and get a medical report if you are hurt.
tips.inPlainWords: You may defend yourself against an immediate attack, but only against the attacker and only with the force needed to stop it. The BNS, 2023 limits private defence to the danger, and it ends when the threat ends. Do not chase or retaliate after the attacker has stopped.
tips.benefit: Sections 34 to 38 of the BNS, 2023 set out the right of private defence, including the limits and the exceptions. The force must be proportionate to the threat; a lethal response to a slap can be excessive. The court decides on the facts, and the burden is on the person claiming the defence. A witness and a prompt police report support the claim.
tips.sources: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (private defence). <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Ministry of Home Affairs. <https://www.mha.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: A weapon changes the assessment. Do not continue after the attacker is disabled or has fled. A claim of self-defence does not cover a pre-arranged fight.

tips.title: Unpaid wages, wrongful dismissal or a financial loss: use the legal route, not revenge
tips.cost: Court fees and a lawyer cost money; legal aid is free for eligible applicants. A demand notice is cheap and can lead to a settlement.
tips.inPlainWords: For unpaid wages, complain to the labour commissioner under the Code on Wages, 2019 or the state Shops and Establishments Act, and keep the appointment letter, wage slips and bank statements. For a wrongful dismissal, a labour court or industrial tribunal can hear the dispute if the employer is covered. For a consumer or contract loss, the consumer commission or a civil court is the route. Revenge turns a claim into a crime.
tips.benefit: The Code on Wages, 2019 provides for claims and recovery of wages, and the Industrial Relations Code, 2020 provides for adjudication of dismissal disputes. The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 covers deficient goods and services. Legal aid is available under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 through NALSA and the district authority. A written notice and a documented claim improve the outcome.
tips.sources: Code on Wages, 2019. <https://labour.gov.in/labour-codes>; Industrial Relations Code, 2020. <https://labour.gov.in/labour-codes>; Consumer Protection Act, 2019. <https://consumeraffairs.nic.in/>; National Legal Services Authority. <https://nalsa.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: The limitation period for a civil claim is generally three years under the Limitation Act, 1963, and labour disputes have their own time limits. Do not destroy or withhold the employer's property as leverage.

tips.title: No matter how angry you are, never target innocent people: deliberately driving into a crowd or committing violence in public is classified as endangering public safety by dangerous means, carrying a minimum sentence of three years; if anyone dies, the penalty is death.
tips.cost: No cost to stop. If you feel you may harm yourself or others, call Tele-MANAS on 14416 or 112 and get away from the trigger.
tips.inPlainWords: However angry you are, never target people who had nothing to do with the dispute. Driving into a crowd, attacking a school or a workplace, or setting a fire is mass harm, and the BNS, 2023 punishes murder, attempted murder and acts endangering public safety with the heaviest penalties. Innocent people pay for a quarrel they never knew about.
tips.benefit: The BNS, 2023 contains offences for murder, culpable homicide, attempt and acts endangering life or public safety, with the most serious penalties. The court can award compensation to the victims. A grievance, however real, is not a defence to an attack on uninvolved people. The law also provides for mental-health support and legal aid.
tips.sources: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Tele-MANAS. <https://telemanas.mohfw.gov.in/>; Ministry of Home Affairs. <https://www.mha.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Threats posted online are evidence and can lead to arrest. If you are in crisis, ask a friend to stay with you and go to a hospital.

tips.title: Thoughts such as “find a scapegoat” or “die together” must be treated as a medical emergency: leave the scene, hand over car keys and knives to someone else, and call 14416 (Tele-MANAS).
tips.cost: The helpline is free. A government hospital psychiatric consultation is free or charged at the outpatient rate.
tips.inPlainWords: Thoughts of 'finding a scapegoat' or 'dying together' are a mental-health emergency, not a plan. Leave the scene, call Tele-MANAS on 14416 or 112, and tell someone nearby. A hospital psychiatric emergency can help. The BNS, 2023 punishes homicide and hurt, and a crisis is not a legal defence to harming someone else.
tips.benefit: Tele-MANAS runs a 24-hour national mental-health helpline on 14416 with state cells. A district hospital or medical college has a psychiatry department. The Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 gives a person the right to access care and to make an advance directive. The BNS, 2023 punishes murder, hurt and criminal intimidation; a mental-health condition is dealt with at trial, not by taking it out on others.
tips.sources: Tele-MANAS. <https://telemanas.mohfw.gov.in/>; Mental Healthcare Act, 2017. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. <https://mohfw.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: A crisis can pass; a violent act cannot be undone. If someone is in immediate danger, call 112. Do not stay alone with a weapon.

tips.title: When a family member says 'no one will be safe' or 'I'll take the children', treat it as a danger signal and act
tips.cost: No cost. A protection officer and legal aid are available. Keep the messages, the dates and any witness details.
tips.inPlainWords: A threat to kill, to take the children or to burn the house is not just anger. Call 112, keep a record of the messages, and contact the protection officer under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 or the district child protection unit. A court can grant a protection order, a residence order and custody. Do not wait for the threat to become an act.
tips.benefit: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 provides protection, residence, monetary relief and custody orders, and the police must register an FIR for a cognisable offence. The Juvenile Justice Act, 2015 protects a child in need of care. The BNS, 2023 punishes criminal intimidation and hurt. A written complaint and a medical or police record are strong evidence.
tips.sources: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Ministry of Women and Child Development. <https://wcd.gov.in/>; Childline 1098. <https://childlineindia.org.in/>; National Legal Services Authority. <https://nalsa.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: A family threat can escalate quickly. Have a safe place and a bag ready. Do not confront the person alone. If a child is in danger, call 1098.

tips.title: Don’t curse, spread rumors, or share unverified content online; if you’re a victim of online abuse, document evidence first then report it to police
tips.cost: No cost. Keep the evidence and a diary of the abuse. Do not respond in kind.
tips.inPlainWords: Do not curse, spread rumours or share unverified content about a person. If you are the target, document the posts with screenshots, URLs and dates, report to the platform, and complain to the police or the cyber crime portal. Defamation and criminal intimidation are offences under the BNS, 2023, and the IT Act covers electronic abuse.
tips.benefit: The BNS, 2023 contains offences for defamation, criminal intimidation and insulting a person. The IT Act, 2000 covers obscene publication and identity misuse. The platform's grievance officer must act on a complaint under the IT Rules, 2021. A civil suit for damages is possible. A sustained campaign can also be treated as stalking or harassment.
tips.sources: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Information Technology Act, 2000. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal. <https://cybercrime.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: A public figure has a lower expectation of privacy but still protects against false statements. A joke can be defamation if it is presented as fact. If the abuse includes a sexual image, report it immediately and do not forward it.

tips.title: Read the document thoroughly before signing; never sign on behalf of others or on blank paper
tips.cost: No cost. Ask for the full document and 24 hours to read it. A lawyer's review of a property or loan document is worth the fee.
tips.inPlainWords: Read a contract before you sign it, and never sign a blank page or a document you do not understand. Under the Indian Contract Act, 1872, a contract signed without free consent can be voidable, but proving coercion or fraud later is hard. Sign each page, keep a copy, and do not sign on someone else's behalf without a written power of attorney.
tips.benefit: The Indian Contract Act, 1872 governs offer, acceptance and consideration, and allows a contract to be avoided where consent was obtained by coercion, undue influence, fraud or misrepresentation. A blank signature page can be filled in later; a copy stamped and signed on every page is evidence of what you agreed. A power of attorney must be in writing and, for immovable property, registered. A guarantor is bound by the guarantee terms, not by a verbal assurance.
tips.sources: Indian Contract Act, 1872. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Registration Act, 1908. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Powers of Attorney Act, 1882. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: A document in a language you do not read should be translated. Do not sign a 'standard form' without reading the termination and penalty clauses. A witnessed signature is stronger evidence.

tips.title: Write a clear loan agreement when lending money; think carefully before agreeing to be a guarantor
tips.cost: A stamp paper and a lawyer's fee are small compared with losing the money. Keep the bank transfer record, not just cash.
tips.inPlainWords: When you lend money, write a loan agreement with the amount, the interest, the repayment date and the account details. A promissory note or a cheque helps. Think hard before becoming a guarantor: under the Indian Contract Act, 1872, the surety is liable to the creditor, and a verbal assurance is not a limit on that liability.
tips.benefit: The Indian Contract Act, 1872 governs loans and guarantees. A guarantee can be limited to a fixed amount or period; a continuing guarantee can be revoked for future transactions by notice. A cheque that bounces can support a complaint under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881. The limitation period for a money claim is generally three years from the due date under the Limitation Act, 1963.
tips.sources: Indian Contract Act, 1872. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Limitation Act, 1963. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: Interest income is taxable, and a cash loan above the prescribed limit can attract tax scrutiny. Do not lend to a stranger who offers a high return. A guarantor should get a copy of the loan agreement.

tips.title: Know the time limits: three years for most civil claims, two years for a consumer complaint, and shorter deadlines for some labour claims
tips.cost: Court fees and a lawyer; legal aid is available. A demand notice is cheaper and may restart the negotiation.
tips.inPlainWords: A civil suit for money or breach of contract is generally barred after three years from the date the right to sue arises under the Limitation Act, 1963. A consumer complaint must be filed within two years of the defect or deficiency. Labour and wage claims have their own limitation under the labour codes. A written demand can interrupt the limitation period in some cases. Do not sit on a claim.
tips.benefit: The Limitation Act, 1963 sets the periods: three years for a money claim or breach of contract, twelve years for immovable property, and shorter periods for some claims. The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 sets two years for a consumer complaint, with a condonation application for delay. The Code on Wages, 2019 and the Industrial Relations Code, 2020 set their own limits for wage and dismissal disputes. A suit filed after the period can be dismissed if the defendant raises limitation.
tips.sources: Limitation Act, 1963. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Consumer Protection Act, 2019. <https://consumeraffairs.nic.in/>; Code on Wages, 2019. <https://labour.gov.in/labour-codes>; National Legal Services Authority. <https://nalsa.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: The court does not apply the limitation bar on its own; the defendant must raise it. A payment or a written acknowledgement can restart the clock. Keep the date of the demand and the reply.

tips.title: If you’re being sued or have a court order against you, report all your assets truthfully and repay as much as you can — don’t transfer your house or money to relatives, friends, or companies.
tips.cost: Court fees and a lawyer. An insolvency professional costs money. Concealment costs more.
tips.inPlainWords: If you are sued or a court order is passed against you, disclose your assets truthfully and pay what you can. Hiding a bank account, transferring property to a relative or failing to appear can lead to attachment, arrest and contempt under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. An honest statement and a repayment plan are better than concealment.
tips.benefit: Order 21 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 sets out execution: attachment of bank accounts, salary and property, and arrest in some cases. A false affidavit of assets can lead to prosecution for perjury under the BNS, 2023. The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 provides a structured route where the debt cannot be paid. A judgment debtor who cooperates may get an instalment order.
tips.sources: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016. <https://ibbi.gov.in/>; Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: Do not transfer property after the suit is filed; the transfer can be set aside as fraudulent. A family settlement should be documented. Take advice before signing a settlement.

tips.title: If your accounts are attached or you are on a defaulter list, find out which order applies before you act
tips.cost: A lawyer's fee; the bank's response is free. Do not pay a commission to 'unfreeze' an account.
tips.inPlainWords: A bank freeze can come from a court attachment, a tax notice, a police complaint or a lender's recovery action. Ask the bank for the order and the authority that issued it. A wilful-defaulter listing by a bank is different from a court decree. Do not pay a 'recovery agent' who cannot show the order. A lawyer can challenge an unlawful attachment.
tips.benefit: Order 21 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 governs attachment, and the Income-tax Act, 1961 and the GST Act give tax authorities powers of attachment. The RBI's wilful-defaulter directions allow banks to publish a list after a review, with a right of representation. The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 provides a resolution route. A bank cannot freeze an account without a lawful basis and must give a reason.
tips.sources: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Reserve Bank of India, wilful defaulters. <https://www.rbi.org.in/>; Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India. <https://ibbi.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: A freeze can be partial or full. A joint account can be affected by one holder's liability. Keep the salary account issue in mind; the bank may release a portion for living expenses.

tips.title: If scammed while shopping online or via second-hand markets, first file a complaint with the platform, then report it to police, and finally decide whether to sue.
tips.cost: A consumer complaint has a small fee; the helpline is free. Keep the evidence.
tips.inPlainWords: If an online purchase goes wrong, first use the platform's grievance officer and keep the order, payment and chat records. If that fails, complain to the consumer commission or the National Consumer Helpline on 1915. For a card or UPI fraud, ask the bank for a chargeback and report on 1930. Do not send more money to 'release' a refund.
tips.benefit: The Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 require a marketplace to appoint a grievance officer and disclose the seller. The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 allows a complaint before the district, state or national commission depending on the value, within two years. The RBI's chargeback rules apply to card and UPI transactions. The BNS, 2023 covers cheating.
tips.sources: Consumer Protection Act, 2019. <https://consumeraffairs.nic.in/>; Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020. <https://consumeraffairs.nic.in/>; National Consumer Helpline. <https://consumerhelpline.gov.in/>; Reserve Bank of India, chargebacks. <https://www.rbi.org.in/>
tips.caveats: A marketplace and a seller are separate; the platform may not be liable for every seller. A 'no refund' clause does not override the consumer law. Do not accept a settlement that requires you to withdraw the complaint before payment.

tips.title: Think carefully before and after making large gifts in romantic relationships or marriage
tips.cost: Stamp duty and registration fees for property; a written agreement costs little. Keep the bank record.
tips.inPlainWords: A large gift to a partner is a transfer of property, not a guarantee of marriage. If the relationship ends, the law will ask what the transfer was for: a gift, a loan, a joint purchase or a conditional transfer. Write down the purpose, keep the payment trail and, for immovable property, register the transfer. Do not rely on a verbal promise.
tips.benefit: The Indian Contract Act, 1872, the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 and the Registration Act, 1908 govern gifts and transfers. A gift of immovable property must be registered. A loan should be documented with the repayment terms. The Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 prohibits a demand for dowry. The court can look at the conduct and the documents, not only the label.
tips.sources: Transfer of Property Act, 1882. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Registration Act, 1908. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: A gift is generally irrevocable once made. A conditional gift can be recovered only if the condition is proved. A public accusation without evidence can be defamation.

tips.title: Dowry is prohibited: never demand or pay it, and record money transfers by bank
tips.cost: No cost to refuse. A lawyer's fee if a complaint is filed; legal aid is available.
tips.inPlainWords: The Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 prohibits giving, taking or demanding dowry, and the BNS, 2023 punishes cruelty and dowry death. A demand for money, a car or property as a condition of marriage is an offence. If money is transferred for a genuine purpose, use a bank transfer with a note and keep the record. Do not use cash or a third-party account.
tips.benefit: The Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 provides imprisonment and a fine for giving or taking dowry and for demanding it. The BNS, 2023 contains offences for dowry death and cruelty by a husband or his relatives. A complaint can be filed by the victim, a relative or a recognised welfare organisation. A bank record and a written list of gifts help distinguish a voluntary gift from a demand.
tips.sources: Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Ministry of Women and Child Development. <https://wcd.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: A wedding gift given voluntarily is not dowry, but a demand made before or after the marriage can be. A 'gift list' demanded by one family is evidence. Do not destroy the messages.

tips.title: No need to worry about premarital assets — clearly define property additions and parental contributions
tips.cost: A lawyer and a registered deed cost money; a written record costs little. Keep the bank statements.
tips.inPlainWords: Property owned before marriage generally remains separate under Indian personal law, but commingling, joint names and a failure to document contributions can change the picture. Keep the title documents, the payment trail and a written record of any family contribution. A prenuptial agreement is not automatically enforceable in India, so do not rely on one alone.
tips.benefit: The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, the Special Marriage Act, 1954 and the Indian Succession Act, 1925 govern property and succession for different communities. A gift or inheritance can be separate property, but placing it in a joint account or a joint name can create a dispute. The court can consider the source of the funds and the intention. A registered gift deed or a clear will reduces uncertainty.
tips.sources: Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Special Marriage Act, 1954. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Indian Succession Act, 1925. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: A prenuptial agreement is not a recognized category with automatic enforceability; a court may consider it as evidence of intention. A joint home loan creates rights and liabilities. Do not transfer a family property without advice.

tips.title: Check a person’s marital status before getting married; those who use marriage as a pretext to defraud money can be prosecuted for fraud.
tips.cost: No cost to ask. A lawyer's check of the divorce decree or the marriage record is cheap.
tips.inPlainWords: Before you marry, check the person's marital status and identity. Bigamy is an offence under the BNS, 2023, and using a false identity or a false promise of marriage to obtain money can be cheating. A marriage under the Special Marriage Act, 1954 requires a notice, which gives time for an objection. Ask for the divorce decree where a previous marriage ended.
tips.benefit: The BNS, 2023 punishes bigamy and cheating. The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 and the Special Marriage Act, 1954 set the conditions for a valid marriage, including that neither party has a living spouse. A marriage in violation is void. A false promise of marriage can be cheating where the intention was to obtain money or property. The Special Marriage Act notice is public and allows objections.
tips.sources: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Special Marriage Act, 1954. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: A divorce decree from another country may need recognition in India. A religious marriage may not be registered; check the applicable law. Do not confront the person alone if you suspect fraud; keep the evidence.

tips.title: For home appliance repairs, vehicle inspections, and renovations: always ask for a quote first and stay on site throughout the process.
tips.cost: No cost to ask for an estimate. A second opinion costs less than a bad repair.
tips.inPlainWords: For a repair, an inspection or a renovation, ask for a written estimate before the work starts and keep the old parts. Pay in stages, not all upfront, and get a receipt for every payment. If the work is defective, the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 gives you a remedy; a verbal quote is hard to prove.
tips.benefit: The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 covers deficient service and unfair trade practice. A written estimate, the scope of work and the warranty terms are the evidence. The invoice must show the GSTIN and the tax; a cash payment without a bill weakens the claim. A manufacturer's warranty is separate from the repairer's workmanship warranty.
tips.sources: Consumer Protection Act, 2019. <https://consumeraffairs.nic.in/>; National Consumer Helpline. <https://consumerhelpline.gov.in/>; Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs. <https://www.cbic.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: A 'minimum charge' can become a large bill. Do not sign a blank job card. If the repairer keeps the vehicle, get a receipt with the odometer reading.

tips.title: Don’t be a “nominal legal representative” — don’t lend your ID to register a company
tips.cost: No cost to refuse. A lawyer's fee if you are already a director and want to resign.
tips.inPlainWords: Do not become a nominal director or shareholder for someone else. Under the Companies Act, 2013, a director has statutory duties and can be disqualified, fined or prosecuted for the company's defaults. Lending your DIN, PAN or Aadhaar to register a company can make you liable for its taxes, filings and fraud.
tips.benefit: The Companies Act, 2013 imposes duties on directors and provides for disqualification under section 164 for failure to file returns, and for prosecution for fraud. A director can be liable for the company's tax and provident-fund defaults. The benami law can apply where shares are held for another. A resignation must be filed with the ROC to be effective.
tips.sources: Companies Act, 2013. <https://www.mca.gov.in/>; Benami Transactions (Prohibition) Act, 1988. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Ministry of Corporate Affairs. <https://www.mca.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: A 'sleeping director' is still a director in law. Resigning without filing Form DIR-11 leaves you on record. Do not sign a blank board resolution.

tips.title: Don’t carry items for strangers when traveling, and don’t accept packages of unknown origin
tips.cost: No cost to refuse. A locked bag and a baggage tag cost little.
tips.inPlainWords: Never carry a parcel, envelope or bag for a stranger, however friendly or well-dressed, and never accept a package whose contents you have not seen. If you are stopped at an airport or a border with drugs or contraband, the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985 and the Customs Act, 1962 can apply regardless of whether you knew. Keep your luggage locked and in sight.
tips.benefit: The NDPS Act, 1985 provides severe punishment for possession and transport of narcotics, and the Customs Act, 1962 covers smuggling. The carrier is presumed to know what is in the baggage in many cases, and a claim of ignorance is a weak defence. Airlines and airports publish warnings against carrying packages for others. A sealed parcel from an unknown person is a red flag.
tips.sources: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Customs Act, 1962. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Bureau of Civil Aviation Security. <https://www.bcasindia.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: A 'gift for a relative' can be a trap. Do not leave your bag unattended. If a co-passenger asks you to watch a bag, refuse and call security.

tips.title: Leash the dog: if it injures someone, the owner is liable, and a local leash rule removes most defences
tips.cost: A leash, a muzzle and vaccination cost little. A civil claim can be expensive.
tips.inPlainWords: Under the law of torts, the owner or keeper of an animal is liable for harm it causes, and many municipal and housing-society rules require a leash in public. If the owner ignored a safety rule, a claim of the victim's negligence is harder to sustain. Keep the dog leashed, vaccinate it, and register it where the local body requires.
tips.benefit: The owner or person in charge of an animal is liable in tort for damage caused by it. The Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960 and the state municipal laws set duties for pet owners, and many states and societies require a leash and a muzzle for a dangerous breed. The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 does not apply to a pet injury, but a civil suit for damages does. The owner can also face a police complaint under the BNS, 2023 for a negligent act.
tips.sources: Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying. <https://dahd.nic.in/>; Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: A victim who trespasses or provokes the dog may reduce the claim, but not the leash duty. A stray dog is a municipal responsibility. Report a biting dog to the local body and the police.

tips.title: If the other person is intoxicated, unconscious, or under 14, do not have sex with them
tips.cost: No cost. If you or someone else is at risk, call 112 or 1091 (women's helpline).
tips.inPlainWords: If a person is intoxicated, unconscious or asleep, they cannot consent to sex. Under the BNS, 2023, sex without valid consent is rape or sexual assault, and a person under 18 is protected by the POCSO Act, 2012. A prior relationship or a message does not create consent for a later act. If you are unsure, stop.
tips.benefit: The BNS, 2023 defines consent as a free and voluntary agreement, and a person who is intoxicated or unconscious cannot give it. The POCSO Act, 2012 protects a child under 18. The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 and the BNSS, 2023 set the procedure for a complaint and medical examination. A delay in reporting does not destroy the case, but it should be explained.
tips.sources: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Ministry of Women and Child Development. <https://wcd.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: A person who is drunk can still be the accused; intoxication is not a defence to a sexual offence. Do not share the complainant's identity. Take a medical examination and preserve the clothes if you are the victim.

tips.title: If someone threatens to call the police, post intimate photos, or inform your workplace unless you pay up — don’t give them a single cent and don’t delete any records; call the police right away.
tips.cost: No cost. Do not pay, do not send more photos, and do not delete the evidence.
tips.inPlainWords: If someone threatens to post intimate photos, tell your workplace or call the police unless you pay, that is extortion and criminal intimidation under the BNS, 2023, and the IT Act covers the publication of private images. Do not pay. Save the messages, the account and the payment demand, report on 1930 and cybercrime.gov.in, and ask the platform to take the content down.
tips.benefit: The BNS, 2023 punishes extortion, criminal intimidation and the publication of obscene material. The IT Act, 2000 covers publishing or transmitting private images and identity misuse. The platform's grievance officer must act under the IT Rules, 2021. A payment often leads to a larger demand; a police report and a takedown request are the effective steps. The victim's identity is protected in a sexual-offence case.
tips.sources: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Information Technology Act, 2000. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal. <https://cybercrime.gov.in/>; Ministry of Women and Child Development. <https://wcd.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: A fake profile can be reported and traced. Tell a trusted person and keep your phone secure. If the content is already public, ask the platform for an urgent takedown and a court injunction.

tips.title: If someone falsely accuses you, you can seek legal consequences: up to 5 days of detention for minor violations, up to 3 years in prison for criminal acts
tips.cost: A lawyer's fee; legal aid is available. Keep the records; a verbal accusation is harder to prove.
tips.inPlainWords: If someone falsely accuses you, keep the complaint, the messages and the witness details. A false accusation can be defamation under the BNS, 2023, and a false statement in a judicial proceeding can be an offence. You can file a civil suit for damages and a criminal complaint. Do not retaliate with a false counter-complaint.
tips.benefit: The BNS, 2023 contains offences for defamation and for giving false evidence. The BNSS, 2023 allows a complaint to a magistrate and an appeal against a wrongful order. A civil defamation suit can seek damages and an injunction. The truth is a defence to defamation, and the burden is on the person making the statement. A malicious prosecution can support a claim for damages.
tips.sources: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; National Legal Services Authority. <https://nalsa.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: A complaint to the police is not automatically defamation; the person may have a reasonable belief. Do not publish the accuser's details online; that can be a fresh offence.

tips.title: Insufficient evidence alone warrants acquittal; coerced confessions must be excluded; appeals and retrials remain possible after conviction
tips.cost: A lawyer's fee; legal aid is available. A private investigator is not necessary in most cases.
tips.inPlainWords: A confession made under coercion is not admissible, and a case built only on suspicion should fail. The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 and the BNSS, 2023 set the rules for evidence, bail and appeal. If you are accused, do not sign a statement you did not make; ask for a lawyer, and preserve the CCTV, the messages and the witnesses.
tips.benefit: The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 governs the admissibility of evidence, and a confession to a police officer is not admissible. The BNSS, 2023 provides for bail, appeal and revision. The Supreme Court has held that suspicion cannot replace proof. An acquittal can be appealed by the state, so keep the record. A lawyer can challenge a defective investigation.
tips.sources: Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Supreme Court of India. <https://www.sci.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: An alibi needs evidence, not just a statement. Do not tamper with a witness. A retrial is not automatic; an appeal must show a legal error.

tips.title: For individuals released from detention after a case is dropped, charges are withdrawn, or they are acquitted, applying for state compensation is possible — compensation is calculated on a daily basis.
tips.cost: A lawyer's fee; legal aid is available. Keep the acquittal order and the medical and wage records.
tips.inPlainWords: If a case against you is dropped or you are acquitted, you may be entitled to compensation for a wrongful arrest or prosecution under the BNSS, 2023 and the Supreme Court's guidelines. The compensation is not automatic; you must apply to the court or the legal services authority with the order and the proof of loss. A civil suit against the state is a separate route.
tips.benefit: Section 396 of the BNSS, 2023 provides for compensation to a victim, and the Supreme Court's decisions on compensation for wrongful arrest set the principles. The Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 and NALSA can help with the application. A suit against the state under the law of torts requires proof of malice or a gross illegality. The court can also order the return of seized property.
tips.sources: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; National Legal Services Authority. <https://nalsa.gov.in/>; Supreme Court of India. <https://www.sci.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: An acquittal does not automatically mean the arrest was illegal. A compensation claim can take years. Do not sign a release without advice.

tips.title: If you’re a victim seeking compensation, use channels like 1915 (National Consumer Helpline), file a lawsuit, or hire a lawyer. Never meet the offending party alone, and don’t phrase “paying money” and “I won’t expose you” as a single condition.
tips.cost: Legal aid is free for eligible applicants. A private lawyer costs money; a written settlement can save time.
tips.inPlainWords: As a victim, use the legal channels: the police, the victim compensation scheme under the BNSS, 2023, the consumer commission, a civil suit or NALSA legal aid on 15100. Do not meet the accused alone to negotiate, and do not accept a cash settlement without a written order. A lawyer or a legal-aid volunteer can attend with you.
tips.benefit: The BNSS, 2023 provides for victim compensation and the restitution of property. The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 covers deficient services and products. The Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 provides free legal aid to eligible victims. A civil suit can claim damages. The court can order a compensation payment as part of the sentence. A written settlement filed in court is enforceable; a private cash deal is not.
tips.sources: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Consumer Protection Act, 2019. <https://consumeraffairs.nic.in/>; National Legal Services Authority. <https://nalsa.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: A settlement in a serious offence needs the court's permission. Do not withdraw an FIR before you receive the compensation. Keep the medical and loss records.

tips.title: Cyberbullying: First enable protections, gather evidence, then choose between court injunctions, private prosecution, or police reports
tips.cost: No cost to report. A lawyer's fee for an injunction.
tips.inPlainWords: If you are being cyberbullied, first use the platform's block, mute and report tools, then save the screenshots, URLs and dates. Report to the platform's grievance officer under the IT Rules, 2021, and to the police or cybercrime.gov.in if there is a threat or a sexual image. A court can grant an injunction and damages.
tips.benefit: The IT Act, 2000 and the IT Rules, 2021 require a platform to act on a grievance. The BNS, 2023 covers defamation, criminal intimidation and stalking. The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 allows electronic evidence with a certificate. A civil suit can seek an injunction and damages. A sustained campaign can also be reported to the National Commission for Women.
tips.sources: Information Technology Act, 2000. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal. <https://cybercrime.gov.in/>; National Commission for Women. <https://ncw.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: Do not engage with the abuser. A screenshot without the URL and date is weaker evidence. If the abuse includes a morphed image, report it as a sexual offence.

tips.title: The legal route of “buying insurance for a family member first, then harming them” is completely blocked: you get zero money, and the perpetrator faces multiple charges including intentional homicide and insurance fraud.
tips.cost: No cost. Do not sign a proposal form for a person who does not consent. A policy on another adult needs their consent and, often, a medical examination.
tips.inPlainWords: You cannot insure a person and then harm them for the payout. Murder is the gravest offence under the BNS, 2023, and a person who causes the death of the insured cannot claim the benefit. The insurer will investigate, and the nominee or beneficiary who is involved forfeits the claim. The policy does not legalize the act.
tips.benefit: The BNS, 2023 punishes murder and abetment. The Insurance Act, 1938 and the policy terms exclude a claim where the beneficiary caused the death. The insurer can repudiate the claim and report the matter to the police. A nominee who is complicit can be prosecuted and cannot profit from the crime. The court can order the return of the premium or the policy to the lawful heir.
tips.sources: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Insurance Act, 1938. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India. <https://irdai.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: A policy on a child is restricted. A 'keyman' policy is for a business, not a licence to harm. If you suspect a policy fraud, report it to the insurer and the police.

tips.title: You must obtain a case receipt when reporting a crime; if no case is opened, you must receive a written notice. You can request a reconsideration within 7 days and a review within another 7 days. The procuratorate can also order the police to open a case.
tips.cost: No cost. The FIR copy is free. A lawyer's fee if you need to apply to the magistrate.
tips.inPlainWords: When you report a crime, ask for the FIR to be registered and get a free copy. Under the BNSS, 2023, the police must register an FIR for a cognisable offence and give you a copy. If they refuse, write to the Superintendent of Police and, if that fails, apply to the magistrate. A receipt with the FIR number is your proof.
tips.benefit: Section 173 of the BNSS, 2023 requires the officer in charge to register an FIR and give a copy to the informant free of cost. Section 175 allows a complaint to the Superintendent of Police and then to the magistrate. The BNSS provides for the registration of a zero FIR at any police station. An acknowledgement is essential for a compensation or insurance claim.
tips.sources: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Ministry of Home Affairs. <https://www.mha.gov.in/>; National Legal Services Authority. <https://nalsa.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: A police station cannot refuse an FIR because the offence happened in another area; it can register a zero FIR and transfer it. Keep the date and the officer's name.

tips.title: Don’t give money or cards to investigators, law enforcers: offering bribes is a crime, and bribing oversight, law enforcement, and judicial staff is punished even more severely.
tips.cost: No cost to refuse. A lawyer's fee for the case.
tips.inPlainWords: Never offer money or a gift to a police officer or a public servant to avoid a case or get a favour. Offering a bribe is an offence under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, even if the officer refuses, and it can be prosecuted under the BNS, 2023. Use the lawful route: a lawyer, a complaint to the senior officer or the anti-corruption bureau.
tips.benefit: The Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 punishes a public servant who accepts a bribe and a person who offers one. The BNS, 2023 covers abetment and criminal conspiracy. The Central Vigilance Commission and the state anti-corruption bureaus investigate complaints. A bribe creates a record and can be used against you. A lawful complaint is protected.
tips.sources: Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Central Vigilance Commission. <https://cvc.gov.in/>; Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: A 'speed money' demand can be reported to the anti-corruption helpline. Do not pay and then complain; the payment itself is evidence against you.

tips.title: For calls and in-person talks where things might turn sour, start recording right away: you can record conversations you personally take part in without needing prior consent from the other party.
tips.cost: No cost. A forensic certificate may cost money if the recording is disputed.
tips.inPlainWords: You can record a conversation you are part of, and the recording can be used as evidence if it is genuine and relevant; a secret recording of a private conversation you are not part of is riskier. Keep the original file, do not edit it, and tell the court how it was made. Do not publish it online.
tips.benefit: The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 allows electronic evidence with a certificate, and the Supreme Court has admitted a bona fide recording of a conversation to which the recorder was a party. The right to privacy under Article 21 restricts a secret recording of a third party. Publishing an intimate image is an offence under the IT Act and the BNS. A transcript and the original device strengthen the evidence.
tips.sources: Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Information Technology Act, 2000. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Supreme Court of India. <https://www.sci.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: A recording obtained by trespass or coercion may be excluded. Do not record a privileged lawyer-client conversation. A phone recording can be erased; back it up.

tips.title: In an emergency at the scene, first film a wide shot, then capture the spatial relationships, and finally record the damage and injuries — keep the original photos and videos.
tips.cost: No cost. A phone camera and a backup are enough.
tips.inPlainWords: At an accident or a crime scene, first make sure you are safe and call 112. Then take a wide shot, a mid shot and a close-up, and note the time and place. Do not move evidence or block the police. Give the footage to the investigating officer and keep a copy.
tips.benefit: The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 treats electronic records as evidence with a certificate, and a contemporaneous video is strong evidence of the scene. The BNSS, 2023 requires a person to cooperate with an investigation. Obstructing a public servant is an offence under the BNS, 2023. A video can also help an insurance or compensation claim.
tips.sources: Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Ministry of Road Transport and Highways. <https://morth.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: Do not film an injured person's face for social media. Do not edit or filter the video. A wide shot that shows the road and the vehicles is more useful than a close-up of the damage.

tips.title: Domestic violence: call 112 or 181, get a medical record, and apply for a protection order
tips.cost: No cost for the protection officer or legal aid. A private lawyer costs money.
tips.inPlainWords: Domestic violence is not a private matter. The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 provides protection, residence, monetary relief and custody orders, and the police must register an FIR for a cognisable offence. Call 112 or the women's helpline 181, get a medical examination, and keep the messages and the dates. A protection officer can help you apply to the magistrate.
tips.benefit: The 2005 Act covers physical, sexual, verbal, emotional and economic abuse, and allows a woman to stay in the shared household. The magistrate can grant a protection order, a residence order, a restraint order and monetary relief. The BNSS, 2023 and the BNS, 2023 apply to the criminal offence. A medical report and a diary of incidents are strong evidence. Legal aid is available through NALSA.
tips.sources: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Ministry of Women and Child Development. <https://wcd.gov.in/>; National Legal Services Authority. <https://nalsa.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: A protection order can be enforced by the police. Do not confront the abuser alone. Keep a safe place and a bag ready. A child in the home is also protected under the JJ Act, 2015.

tips.title: Do not rush to pay a family member's gambling debt: a wager is not enforceable, and it is not a joint marital debt
tips.cost: A lawyer's fee. Do not pay a 'settlement' to a collector without a written agreement and advice.
tips.inPlainWords: Under section 30 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, a wager is void and a court will not enforce a gambling debt. A loan made for gambling may also be unenforceable if the lender knew the purpose. A debt incurred by one spouse for gambling is not automatically a joint debt. Do not pay a debt collector without a court order or legal advice.
tips.benefit: Section 30 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872 makes a wagering agreement void, and no suit lies to recover a wager. A loan advanced for an illegal purpose can be refused recovery under the Act. The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 and the Special Marriage Act, 1954 do not make a spouse liable for the other's independent tort or crime. The BNS, 2023 covers extortion and criminal intimidation if a collector threatens you.
tips.sources: Indian Contract Act, 1872 (section 30). <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: A debt for necessities can be different. A joint account or a joint loan creates a separate liability. If a collector threatens you, call 112 and report it.

tips.title: If an acquaintance asks you to "help scan your face or act as a witness" for a loan, or asks you to read out an SMS verification code, refuse immediately: this is an "AB Loan" scam where you become the legal borrower, not a guarantor
tips.cost: No cost to refuse. A lawyer's fee if a loan appears in your name.
tips.inPlainWords: If a friend asks you to 'scan your face', 'act as a witness' for a loan or read out a script for a video, stop. A face scan can authorise a loan or a KYC in your name, and a witness signature can make you liable. Never do it for money, and never let anyone use your phone for a 'quick verification'.
tips.benefit: The Aadhaar Act, 2016 and the RBI's KYC rules protect biometric authentication; a face scan can complete an e-KYC and a loan. The BNS, 2023 covers cheating, forgery and impersonation, and the IT Act covers identity theft. A witness to a loan document can be called to court. A video recording can be used to show consent that you did not give.
tips.sources: Aadhaar Act, 2016. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Reserve Bank of India, KYC. <https://www.rbi.org.in/>; Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: A genuine bank officer will not ask for a face scan on a friend's phone. Check your credit report after refusing. Report a fraudulent loan to the bank and the police.

tips.title: Secure doors and windows with proper locks, install an exterior motion-sensor light, and reliably lock up when leaving: physical locks and lighting prevent residential burglary far more effectively than standalone alarms
tips.cost: A good lock and a light cost little. A CCTV system and insurance cost more.
tips.inPlainWords: Secure the doors and windows with good locks, add a motion-sensor light outside, and lock up even when you are at home. Ask the local police station about its beat patrol and keep the emergency number 112 on speed dial. A neighbour who watches the house is the cheapest alarm.
tips.benefit: The BNS, 2023 punishes house-breaking and theft, and the police can register an FIR. A home insurance policy can cover theft and fire; check the exclusions. A CCTV system helps, but it must not film a neighbour's private space. A written inventory and photographs of valuables help a claim.
tips.sources: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Ministry of Home Affairs. <https://www.mha.gov.in/>; Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India. <https://irdai.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Do not hide a spare key outside. A domestic worker or a tenant needs a background check. Report a suspicious person to the police, not to a WhatsApp group.
